name: Hartley Overproduction Gap Under Echo and Resolving Evidence
description: Studies echo states with zero deficit and the one-bit Fork3 overproduction gap. Omega is nonnegative exactly when licensed bits do not exceed Hartley entropy, with optimal stopping cutoffs.

program.name: The Observation Boundary
program.summary: An observer sends states to records, and its boundary is the set of merged pairs: two distinct states with one record, told apart by no record-determined reading, at infinite resolution cost, repaired by one side symbol whose least alphabet is the largest fiber. The license criterion, under which a target is determined exactly when it is constant on the fibers, is proved on arbitrary sets with its lattice, its Bayes-risk and Blackwell comparison, its Beth gap, the echo law and Shannon's secrecy bound.

oneLine: An echo channel leaves a gap equal to the full terminal Hartley entropy, giving a one-bit Fork3 overproduction gap that resolving evidence closes, while Omega stays nonnegative for capacity-compatible channels and stopping becomes optimal past marginal-price cutoffs.
summary: The objects are licensed episodes with answers and raw and licensed emissions, echo and informative states, licensed-channel deficit in nats and bits, terminal Hartley entropy and the Omega gap with its boundary-event predicate, Fork3 raw and licensed relations with echo and resolving channels, role-indexed star and dependency-pair channels, and finite-horizon and stochastic stopping models with marginal-price cutoffs. The questions are when echo forces zero deficit, when the emitted branch entropy exceeds licensed information to give a positive gap and boundary event, how additional evidence changes Omega, how much role resolution closes the gap, and when continued computation stops being worthwhile. A channel-constant conditional has zero deficit, so a zero-deficit channel leaves Omega equal to the Hartley envelope and yields a boundary event when at least two terminals are reachable, while a source-confluent normalizing relation with nonnegative gain yields no boundary event. On Fork3 the echo channel gives deficitBits zero and Omega one with a boundary event, the licensed relation gives Omega zero, and the resolving channel gives deficitBits one with Omega zero and no event, with the evidence chain rule making the Omega change the negative gain change for a one-bit Fork3 drop. Blind role-constant channels differ from fully resolving channels by HBits of the role law with zero residual for uniform laws, the binary case recovering the Fork3 one-bit exchange, while Omega is preserved under relation isomorphism with evidence relabeling but not under forward simulation collapsing terminals and not determined by release data alone, and independent products add Omega while sequential overwrite does not. For stopping, zero value of computation makes positive cost force stopping, finite-horizon and stochastic Bellman values are attained greatest returns that equal immediate stopping under edge and echo-license conditions, and execution-derived marginal-price cutoffs force stopping at and above the cutoff at every horizon against every adaptive policy.
boundary: On the echo and zero-gain side the licensed bits fall short of the terminal Hartley envelope, so Omega is positive and a boundary event holds when strict branching with at least two reachable terminals is present. On the confluent and resolving side the licensed bits meet or exceed the envelope, so Omega is zero or negative with no boundary event, and the obstruction marking the crossing is whether a licensed channel supplies information about the target beyond the direct surface. The crossing is located by the order laws linking nonnegativity to capacity compatibility and boundary events to licensed bits below Hartley, with Fork3 echo at Omega one and resolving or licensed Fork3 at Omega zero as the concrete one-bit instance.

conclusions.statement: For any finite types T, X, W and Cn, any relation R on T, any source, and any μ, ν and r, 0 ≤ overproductionGap R source μ ν r holds if and only if CapacityCompatible R source μ ν r holds.
For any finite types T, X, W and Cn, any relation R on T, any source, and any μ, ν and r, BoundaryEvent R source μ ν r holds if and only if deficitBits μ ν r < terminalHartleyEntropy R source holds.
For any finite types T, X, W and Cn, any relation R on T, any source, and any μ, ν and r, if deficit μ ν r = 0 then overproductionGap R source μ ν r = terminalHartleyEntropy R source.

For any finite types T, X, W and Cn, any relation R on T, any source, and any μ, ν and r, if ∀ w, ∑ c, ν w c = 1 and there is s with ∀ w c, r w c = s w and terminalMultiplicity R source = m, then overproductionGap R source μ ν r = Real.logb 2 (m : Real).
For any finite types T, X, W and Cn, any relation R on T, any source, and any μ, ν and r, if deficit μ ν r = 0 and 2 ≤ terminalMultiplicity R source then BoundaryEvent R source μ ν r holds.

For any finite types T, X, W and Cn, any relation R on T, any source, and any μ, ν and r, if NormalizingAt R source and ConfluentAt R source hold and 0 ≤ deficit μ ν r holds then BoundaryEvent R source μ ν r does not hold.

The conjunction holds: echo deficitBits equals 0, resolving deficitBits equals 1, raw Fork3 gap with echo equals 1, licensed Fork3 gap with echo equals 0, raw Fork3 with echo is a BoundaryEvent, raw Fork3 gap with resolving equals 0, and raw Fork3 with resolving is not a BoundaryEvent.

For any finite type T, any relation R on T, any source, and finite types X0, W0, C0, X1, W1, C1 with μ0, ν0, r0 and μ1, ν1, r1, overproductionGap R source μ1 ν1 r1 = overproductionGap R source μ0 ν0 r0 - incrementalGainBits (deficitBits μ0 ν0 r0) (deficitBits μ1 ν1 r1).
For any finite types T, X, W and Cn, any relation R on T, any source, and any μ, ν and r, GapBelowEnvelope R source μ ν r holds if and only if LicensedGain μ ν r holds.
For any finite types T, X, W and Cn, any relation R on T, any source, and any μ, ν and r, if deficit μ ν r = 0 then BoundaryEvent R source μ ν r holds if and only if BranchingAt R source holds.
Under 1 ≤ m, sum nu = 1 and role-constant hconst, the gap difference between the constant and resolving channels is HBits nu.
Under 1 ≤ m and law hypotheses, resolving gap is zero holds if and only if nu is uniform.

For any finite types A and B, any relations RA and RB, any relation isomorphism e, any source, and any finite X, W, Cn with μ, ν and r, overproductionGap RA source μ ν r = overproductionGap RB (e.toEquiv source) μ ν r.

ForwardSimulation fork3Collapse Fork3Step BoolForkStep holds and overproductionGap Fork3Step Fork3.source unitSurface uniformChannelWeights echoChannel differs from overproductionGap BoolForkStep (fork3Collapse Fork3.source) unitSurface uniformChannelWeights echoChannel.
Under positive costs and arity plus regional inequality benefit plus next stop at most bound plus current stop on AfterCutoff, value equals stop for all n and cutoff states.

openPoints: Echo bridge theorems carry an object witness o₀ as a parameter that does not occur in the zero-deficit or informativeness conclusions.
Countable divergence needs equal total mass, strict positivity of the reference, and summability of the termwise bound, with a mass-one specialization.
Licensed deficit nonnegativity and the conditioning inequality need nonnegative weights with channel laws summing to one.

Hartley-envelope bounds, Shannon-Hartley comparison, uniform-scheduler attainment and independent-product additivity need local normalization, with product entropy additivity also needing normalized channels.
Order characterizations assume finite carriers; negative Omega occurs when licensed bits exceed Hartley, witnessed by a one-terminal resolving chain at minus one and a two-chain product at minus two.

Role laws need arity at least one with normalized weights, zero residual needs nonnegativity, and no role law exists on Fin 0; value-factored channels keep a one-bit gap while resolving channels close it.

RelIso and boundary-iso preservation need fixed evidence, while forward simulation collapsing two terminals to one and release data alone do not preserve or determine Omega, and equal Omega with equal multiplicity does not imply an isomorphism.

Stopping cutoffs need positive unit cost, payload and arity with regional gain-cost inequalities; stochastic echo stopping ignores zero-probability outcomes, and role observation does not replace well-foundedness for termination.

files.summary: Defines countableRoleDivergence as a tsum over any index type and relates it to finite sums and to klFromUniform under a uniform reference. Proves a termwise Gibbs bound and from it nonnegativity under equal total mass, strict positivity, and summability, with a mass-one specialization. Shows divergence vanishes at the reference law and that on finite alphabets it recovers the finite role gap, vanishing exactly at uniformity.
files.conclusion: Countable divergence from a strictly positive reference is nonnegative under equal mass and summability and recovers the finite role gap with equality to zero exactly at uniformity.

files.summary: Defines an abstract record-generating surface and distinction completeness requiring non-null records to come from distinct inputs. Proves equal inputs are inert, every non-null record certifies distinction, and completeness is equivalent to absence of reflexive non-null emissions. Instantiates a concrete surface mapping equal inputs to void and distinct inputs to diff, proves it distinction-complete, and proves self-broadcasts impossible while broadcasts require and are realized by distinct inputs.
files.conclusion: The concrete eqW surface mapping equal inputs to void and distinct inputs to diff is distinction-complete, so equal inputs are inert and broadcasts require distinct inputs.

files.summary: Defines the target conditional induced by a posterior map and a sufficiency certificate identifying a conditional with it. Proves an echo state forces zero licensed-channel deficit for normalized object laws, both directly and for any sufficient conditional. Proves positive deficit forces an informative channel one-way, and combines zero deficit with exclusion of licensed non-null records and false-formal-legitimacy diagnosis under soundness and witnessedness.
files.conclusion: An echo state yields zero deficit for the induced target conditional and, under soundness and witnessedness, no licensed non-null record, with raw non-null emission diagnosed as false formal legitimacy.

files.summary: Defines a depth-one raw emission graph with terminal record nodes and proves records are normal forms with trivial reachability and nonjoinability of distinct records. Proves false formal legitimacy yields a one-step peak with unjoinable targets, three distinct nodes, and nonconfluence at the source. Combines echo, zero deficit, legitimacy failure, nonconfluence and fixed-state dynamics with unbounded mass growth into a single trap theorem and packages all echo laws into an EchoLawCrown held by every episode.
files.conclusion: Echo with raw non-null emission jointly yields zero deficit, false formal legitimacy, source nonconfluence with three distinct nodes, unbounded mass growth and a fixed state with no licensed non-null record at any depth.

files.summary: Defines a licensed emission episode with answers, distinctions, and raw and licensed surfaces, plus echo as object-independence and informativeness as object-sensitivity. Proves echo is equivalent to non-informativeness and, under licensed soundness and witnessedness, that echo states emit no licensed non-null records while any such record forces informativeness. Defines false formal legitimacy and echo dynamics with iterated runs, proving mass grows by steps, state never moves, echo persists, and no licensed non-null record appears at any depth from echo.
files.conclusion: Under licensed soundness and witnessedness, echo states have no licensed non-null records at any run depth while runs gain unbounded mass with a fixed licensing state.

files.summary: Defines the equality-comparator episode with pair states, Boolean probe and answer reading the probe exactly off the diagonal, raw emission of both void and diff, and licensed emission guarded by distinction. Establishes licensed soundness and witnessedness, echo on diagonal pairs and informativeness off the diagonal. Proves raw non-null diagonal emission gives false formal legitimacy and emission-graph nonconfluence, no licensed diagonal record, and trap dynamics with mass n, fixed pair and no licensed record at any depth, jointly nonvacuous given distinct values.
files.conclusion: The equality-comparator episode satisfies soundness and witnessedness, is echo on the diagonal and informative off it, with false legitimacy, fork nonconfluence and fixed trap dynamics on the diagonal.

files.summary: This file builds two echo-law episodes around a quotation peak. The Boolean quoteEpisode answers with the object off peak and with false at peak, with raw and licensed emission relations. The QuoteEvalCfg-based quoteKernelEpisode uses QuoteEvalStar with congruence enabled for raw emissions and disabled for licensed emissions, with null as value void and non-null as diverged. It proves echo at the peak, informativeness off peak, licensed soundness, false formal legitimacy at the peak with no licensed non-null record, a trap run that stays at peak with growing mass, and a combined peak conjunction with nonjoinable raw outcomes; a final bundle records diagonal conclusions from three settings.
files.conclusion: The quotation kernels give false formal legitimacy at the peak with raw reachability to both value void and diverged that do not join while licensed reachability to diverged is absent.

files.summary: For a finite menu of candidate channels with a zero-cost baseline, capacity at budget b is the maximum licensed gain among eligible channels. The file proves capacity is realized, nonnegative, bounded by the envelope, and monotone in budget, with Omega defined as envelope minus capacity antitone in budget. A two-channel one-bit menu illustrates the theory with capacity zero at budget zero and one at budget one.
files.conclusion: Budgeted Omega is antitone in budget, illustrated by the one-bit menu dropping from one to zero as capacity rises from zero to one.

files.summary: Introduces gated readout: a reading branch on the distinction region, a fixed silence answer off it, and two probes separated by the reading. It proves object-witnessed follows, echo holds off the distinction region, with equivalences linking echo to negated distinction and informativeness to distinction, plus licensed-record consequences under soundness. The Boolean comparator has a gated readout with diagonal echo region, while a flip episode shows the condition is sufficient but not necessary.
files.conclusion: Gated readout yields object-witnessed channels with echo holding off the distinction region, realized by the comparator but not necessary as the flip episode shows.

files.summary: The file shows a relation isomorphism with equivalences of finite evidence alphabets preserves Omega by pullback, including identity transport. It shows equal Omega does not imply a relation isomorphism using two finite chains with equal Omega but different cardinalities. It packages preservation as sufficient and Omega equality alone as insufficient for characterizing transport.
files.conclusion: Coupled relabeling preserves Omega, yet two chains share Omega values without any relation isomorphism between them.

files.summary: Defines over-evidence as strictly negative Omega and its magnitude as max zero minus Omega. It proves over-evidence holds just in case evidence exceeds the envelope, with magnitude equal to minus Omega in the negative regime. Finite chain examples give Omega minus one for one chain and minus two for the product, showing the regime is nontrivial.
files.conclusion: Licensed resolving evidence can exceed the terminal envelope, giving Omega minus one on one chain and minus two on the product.

files.summary: The file defines deficitBits for converting licensed deficit from nats to bits, the overproduction gap as terminal Hartley entropy minus licensed bits, and a boundary event as a positive gap. It proves that zero deficit leaves a gap equal to terminal Hartley entropy, that a redundant echo channel forces this case with gap equal to log base 2 of terminal multiplicity, and that two or more reachable terminals then yield a boundary event, while a source-confluent normalizing relation with nonnegative gain never yields one. With explicit unit, uniform, echo and resolving channels it computes zero licensed bits for echo against one licensed bit for resolving, a gap of one for raw Fork3 with echo against zero for licensed Fork3 and for raw Fork3 with resolving, and lifts the echo case to general echo states with a conjoined summary law.
files.conclusion: In general an echo state with normalized weights leaves a gap equal to the full terminal Hartley entropy and gives a boundary event when at least two terminals are reachable, while the Fork3 conjunction records a one-bit gap and boundary event for raw echo evidence against zero gap and no event after licensing or under resolving evidence.

files.summary: Defines finite terminal abstraction as a map sending concrete terminal support onto abstract support with surjectivity. It proves multiplicity, Hartley entropy, and Omega cannot increase under such abstraction with fixed evidence. A Fork3 guard abstraction illustrates the inequality, lowering Omega from one to zero.
files.conclusion: Support-surjective abstraction cannot increase Omega, with the Fork3 guard lowering it from one to zero.

files.summary: The file fixes the operational relation and compares two evidence channels through incremental licensed gain in bits. It proves the Omega change equals the negative gain change, with monotone and strictly monotone drops as gain rises. It instantiates the rule on Fork3 where echo to resolving gives an exact one-bit drop.
files.conclusion: On a fixed relation the Omega difference equals the negative licensed-gain difference, realized as a one-bit Fork3 drop.

files.summary: The file defines strict terminal branching, licensed gain and gap below envelope in their home namespaces. It proves gap below envelope holds exactly when licensed gain is positive, unconditionally. It proves a boundary event holds exactly when strict branching holds on any zero-gain channel, and packages both as a joint concept bridge law.
files.conclusion: Gap below envelope is equivalent to licensed gain and on zero-gain channels boundary event is equivalent to strict branching.

files.summary: The file relabels the binary channel to the frame and active role alphabet with uniform weights and defines role-resolving and role-constant echo channels. It proves role-constant channels have zero gain, gap one and a boundary event on Fork3, while the role-resolving channel supplies one licensed bit with gap zero and no event. It combines these into a one-bit exchange law that also records the actual dependency-pair channel distinguishing frame from active.
files.conclusion: Value-blind role channels have gap one with an event and role-resolving has one licensed bit with gap zero, differing by one bit.

files.summary: The file identifies the dependency-pair evidence with the role-resolving channel and shows value-factored channels are role-constant with gap one. It transports Fork3 gaps to the KO7 local raw relation by relation isomorphism, giving gap one with an event for value-factored channels and gap zero without an event for dependency-pair evidence, with the one-bit difference equal to the Gate branch-entropy difference. It adds finite-protocol readings where the role observation supplies one conditional bit and fixed-value readings supply zero, and notes termination still needs no-fresh-variables and well-founded minimal chains.
files.conclusion: At the KO7 local source value-factored channels have gap one with an event and dependency-pair evidence has gap zero matching the Gate entropy difference, while termination still needs chain well-foundedness.

files.summary: The file introduces a three-node long chain alongside the two-node short chain. It computes terminal multiplicity one and echo Omega zero for both, with different carrier cardinalities ruling out a relation isomorphism. It concludes Omega together with terminal multiplicity does not determine the relation up to isomorphism.
files.conclusion: Both chains have zero Omega and one terminal without any isomorphism, so Omega plus multiplicity is not a complete invariant.

files.summary: Gives a generic lower-bound rule combining an envelope lower bound and an evidence upper bound into an Omega lower bound, with corollaries for positive Omega boundary events and zero-evidence cases. It records a one-bit lower bound for Fork3 under echo evidence. A bridge structure packages lower and upper bounds that together yield a boundary event.
files.conclusion: Envelope lower bounds above evidence upper bounds force positive Omega boundary events, with Fork3 giving a one-bit instance.

files.summary: The file defines capacity compatibility and the positive part of Omega. It characterizes nonnegative, zero, negative gaps and boundary events by comparison of licensed bits with Hartley entropy, with evidence monotonicity toward weaker channels. It gives a one-terminal resolving example with Omega minus one, showing Omega is not globally nonnegative.
files.conclusion: Omega is nonnegative exactly when licensed bits do not exceed Hartley entropy, and a one-terminal resolving example gives minus one.

files.summary: The file defines asynchronous products of relations and independent products of evidence channels with a normalization structure. It proves terminal supports factor as Cartesian products, multiplicities multiply, and Hartley entropy adds under local normalization. It proves direct, licensed, deficit and deficit-bits entropies add for normalized channels, hence Omega adds for independent products. It gives a five-state sequential-overwrite system where the second stage erases the first choice, yielding one bit instead of two, so sequential composition is not additive.
files.conclusion: Independent normalized products add Omega, while sequential overwrite yields one bit instead of two, so additivity holds for independence but fails for sequential composition.

files.summary: The file defines pullback of direct, channel and target probability data along equivalences. It proves mixture and entropy commute with relabeling, hence direct and licensed conditional entropies, deficit and deficit-bits are invariant. Together with relation-isomorphism invariance of Hartley entropy, it proves Omega is preserved under simultaneous operational and evidence relabeling.
files.conclusion: Omega is invariant under simultaneous operational isomorphism and evidence relabeling by equivalences.

files.summary: Defines a resource state by envelope and evidence bits with Omega as their difference, and free moves that do not raise the envelope and do not lower evidence. It proves Omega is monotone under free moves and connects a concrete system to a resource state. Fully warranted states with envelope below evidence have nonpositive Omega and are preserved by free moves, summarized in a resource-theory law.
files.conclusion: Free moves never increase Omega and preserve full warrant, with full warrant equivalent to nonpositive Omega.

files.summary: The file defines the m-ary star relation on Fin (m+1) with uniform role weights and echo versus resolving channels. It proves the star has m terminals and Hartley entropy log2 m when 1 <= m. It proves a role-constant channel leaves Omega equal to log2 m while the resolving channel supplies log2 m bits and closes Omega to zero, so their difference is log2 m, with the binary case recovering the Fork3 one-bit exchange.
files.conclusion: Blind versus resolving role evidence differ by log2 m, with resolving gap zero and binary case recovering the one-bit Fork3 exchange.

files.summary: The file generalizes role exchange from uniform weights to arbitrary laws on Fin m and arbitrary finite role types, proving the blind-minus-resolving difference is HBits of the law. It characterizes zero residual exactly by uniform laws and impossibility on Fin 0. It defines the r-frame duplicator channel, computes its deficit and residual frame-index gap, and bridges occurrences to rewrite rules with a receipt linking counts, payload equality, DP separation, non-factorization, and runtime blindness, plus KL-divergence identities.
files.conclusion: General role exchange equals HBits of the role law with KL-divergence residual, and r-frame duplication leaves frame-index entropy with one frame recovering the one-bit exchange.

files.summary: The file defines reachable terminal points and schedulers as probability masses on that support, with scheduler entropy and Shannon Omega. It proves every scheduler entropy and Shannon gap is at most the Hartley envelope under local normalization, with the uniform scheduler attaining it. When scheduler entropy aligns with direct entropy, the Shannon gap equals licensed residual entropy, giving zero for fully resolving channels, with Fork3 echo one and resolving zero as instances.
files.conclusion: Shannon Omega is bounded by Hartley Omega with uniform attainment, Fork3 echo giving one bit and resolving giving zero.

files.summary: The file proves Hartley entropy and Omega are invariant under relation isomorphism with fixed evidence, and under boundary isomorphism. It defines forward simulation and a Fork3-to-Boolean collapse that is a simulation but maps two terminals to one, changing echo Omega from one to zero. It shows identity release transport coexists with echo versus resolving Omega differing by one bit, so release data alone do not determine Omega.
files.conclusion: Isomorphism preserves Omega while forward simulation collapsing Fork3 to Boolean and release data alone provide counterexamples to preservation and determination.

files.summary: The file defines cumulative carrier burden for payload length L and depth K as the sum of (i+1)*L. It proves additivity in L and the division-free identity that twice the burden equals (K+1)*(K+2)*L, showing linear growth in L and quadratic growth in K. It proves the burden is at least K+1 for positive L, hence exceeds any bound N and any multiple N*H0 for large depth.
files.conclusion: Cumulative burden has closed doubling form and exceeds every bound for large depth.

files.summary: Defines Exogenous as InformativeAt and PersistentExogenous as its Box modality over R-reachable states. Proves persistence is the greatest forward-invariant subpredicate of exogeny and that for exogenous states persistence holds exactly when no reachable state is an echo. Introduces the greatest exogeny-preserving subrelation SafeRel and proves an exogenous source either persists everywhere reachable or reaches an echo emitting no licensed non-null record under LicensedSound and ObjectWitnessed.
files.conclusion: An exogenous source either remains exogenous at every R-reachable state or reaches an echo state emitting no licensed non-null record.

files.summary: Defines determination of a statement by a projection and a reversible versus irreversible layer split. Proves that if all base-derivable statements are determined by the reversible projection then any undetermined statement is not base-derivable, with counter exhaustion determined and wrapper parity undetermined in the wrapper example. Defines projection transactions and proves license step-invariance plus license-determined dimension and witness imply staticity along any trace, with a constant canonical static example and an identity counterexample showing step-invariance is load-bearing. Defines answers with optional provenance span and license, proves the fields independent with witness-first acceptance requiring license, and proves exogenous gain collapses when all data lie in closure with a non-empty off-closure example.
files.conclusion: Statements undetermined by the reversible projection lie outside base derivability, license invariance forces staticity, and provenance and license are mutually non-entailing.

files.summary: Defines quantitative exogeny as nonzero licensed deficit and its persistent form over reachable states, alongside structural exogeny as informativeness. It proves nonzero deficit persists just in case no reachable state has zero deficit, and that nonzero deficit implies structural exogeny under normalized weights, lifted to persistent forms. A point-mass weighting gives zero deficit for any channel, yielding a Boolean off-diagonal state that is structurally exogenous but not quantitatively so.
files.conclusion: Nonzero licensed deficit implies structural exogeny under normalized weights, yet structural exogeny can hold with zero deficit as the Boolean off-diagonal example shows.

files.summary: Defines value-factoring and role splits with an equal, role-split, or value-split trichotomy. Proves exact refuse, lift, and exogeneity characterizations via Bool separators and packages them as two-action boundaries. Instantiates the law payload-generically and for recursor, payload, and located free-recursor generator occurrences with the activity predicate equal to the extraction channel. Adds a cross-axis conjunction with direct-measure grammar closure and naturality non-discrimination.
files.conclusion: A pair is a role split exactly when value-factored maps agree on it while a Bool separator distinguishes it exogenously, realized payload-generically and at located free-recursor generator occurrences.

files.summary: Defines the frame and active occurrences of void with equal value projection and distinct roles. Proves swap invariance, self-test complementarity, fiber characterization, collision, maximal licensed sets with no greatest set, and two-versus-one symbol licensing limits. Proves value-only decoders fail while value-plus-role decoders succeed and combines refusal, separation, licensing, swap, decoding, root reducts, and a one-bit gap into the two-void boundary theorem.
files.conclusion: The frame and active void occurrences share value but differ in role with combined refusal, lift, licensing, swap, decoding and one-bit gap properties.

files.summary: Defines a certificate with six propositional obligations and acceptance as their conjunction. Checks projections to verdict-supported and witness-present and checks rejection when license or costing fails. Verifies the all-true certificate is accepted and the license-missing certificate is rejected with axiom prints.
files.conclusion: The all-true certificate is accepted while any certificate missing license or costing is rejected.

files.summary: Defines a finite-branching echo stopping problem with stop value, current gain, supplied future value and compute cost, plus dynamic and finite-horizon policies that compare stopping with continuation. Proves that zero or nonpositive current gain with positive cost and dominated continuations forces stopping, while a supplied future surplus and a realized two-state transition can make computing optimal. Shows the static decision problem embeds with zero continuation advantage and that horizon values are attained greatest returns independent of the supplied forecast, with exact edge and echo criteria for stopping at all horizons. Extends the theory to finite-support stochastic models with history-dependent policies, attained Bellman values, invariant stopping criteria ignoring zero-probability outcomes, and a three-outcome averaging example.
files.conclusion: Finite-horizon and stochastic Bellman values are attained greatest returns that equal immediate stopping exactly under edge and echo conditions, while future surplus can make computing optimal despite zero current gain.

files.summary: Defines execution-derived cumulative and marginal prices from the live r-ary recursor orbit and a closed-form least cutoff where marginal price reaches a benefit bound, with weak and strict variants. Builds a deterministic next-depth stochastic decision model whose Bellman value equals the maximum over exact stopping-time prefix returns, each realized by a policy that extends depth a chosen number of times. Proves exact one-step and all-horizon stopping criteria, closure of the post-cutoff region, and that the cutoff region forces stopping at every horizon against every adaptive policy while constant benefit below the cutoff continues. Includes arity-zero, zero-payload, zero-price and future-reward controls and a universal policy crown.
files.conclusion: For duplicating recursors the execution-derived marginal price yields an exact least cutoff where stopping is optimal at every horizon, bounds every adaptive policy, and is attained.

files.summary: Defines meta-query states with budget and obligation multisets, a lexicographic rank using Nat order and the Dershowitz-Manna order, and a licensed step that either drops budget or ties budget with strict multiset descent. Proves every licensed edge strictly decreases rank, so the licensed relation is well-founded and has no cycles, and that identity edges and equal-budget equal-obligation edges are never licensed. Exhibits a three-state terminating deliberation reaching a terminal state and a rank-tie pair with different labels that is blocked.
files.conclusion: Licensed deliberation strictly decreases a lexicographic budget and obligation rank, so it is well-founded and never contains identity, rank-tie or cyclic edges.

files.summary: Defines finite decisions, cell and direct losses, best losses, stop and compute expected losses, value of computation and an optimal meta-policy that computes only on strict improvement after cost. Proves that a channel-constant conditional has zero deficit and zero value of computation, so any positive cost forces stopping, reusing the imported licensed-channel deficit. Computes a two-action two-state instance where the copy channel stops at half cost, the revealing channel computes at half cost, ties at unit cost and stops, packaging the half-cost and unit-cost control.
files.conclusion: A channel-constant zero-deficit channel has zero value of computation so any positive cost forces stopping, whereas a revealing channel can make computing optimal at low cost.

files.summary: This file defines accessibility by factorization and a meta-versus-object access model with direct retrieval and sequential uncertainty reduction. It defines arithmetic progress, recovery and history costs and a primitive-duplicator syntax with canonical stages and terminal records. It proves three executable channels recover progress exactly, attain the universal exact-code minimum width, and carry the full prior entropy with zero-posterior Dirac laws.
files.conclusion: The three named channels exactly recover progress with optimal width and carry the full uniform-prior entropy, while history observation incurs quadratic overcost.

files.summary: This file defines the record ArchitecturalOriginAnchor holding six string-typed qualified names for the pre-undecidability fracture and orientation-boundary substrate and its manuscript anchor, and it defines the canonical anchor value used on T3 and T4 emissions. It proves the canonical anchor names a non-empty manuscript reference. It also proves that at the orientation boundary there is no direct whole-term witness, by applying the forward direction of the orientation-boundary characterization.
files.conclusion: At every orientation-boundary instance, no direct whole-term witness exists, so a forced definite verdict claiming direct-interface support is structurally unbacked.

files.summary: Defines the raw whole-term carrier burden Carr_raw(K,b) by recursion on depth K. Proves the division-free closed form 2*carrierRaw L K = (K+1)*(K+2)*L by induction and monotonicity in K.
files.conclusion: Raw carrier burden has division-free closed form 2*carrierRaw L K = (K+1)*(K+2)*L and is monotone in depth.

files.summary: Defines a sound-and-complete Nat-indexed semidecider interface and jointly total equality and disequality families. Proves the forward collapse manufactures DecidableEq by bounded Nat.find search and the converse manufactures the pair from DecidableEq. Packages the equivalence, instantiates it on Nat, and records an exact comparator as the synchronous special case.
files.conclusion: DecidableEq holds exactly when a jointly total equality and disequality semidecider pair exists.

files.summary: Defines finite conditional entropy as a Y-weighted average, the marginal mixture, and the assembled joint law. Proves the conditioning inequality H(X|Y) ≤ H(X) by concave Jensen and the entropy chain rule H(X,Y)=H(Y)+H(X|Y).
files.conclusion: Conditioning cannot increase entropy and joint entropy splits as H(Y)+H(X|Y).

files.summary: Defines the three confluence-axis forced behaviors and proves exhaustiveness. Proves a committed non-null diagonal record is unlicensed false legitimacy and no licensed diagonal record exists. Packages non-confluence, no record, and guard restoration as the forced trilemma with a void witness.
files.conclusion: At eqW a a the engine is non-confluent, admits no licensed distinction record, and the guard restores confluence off diagonal.

files.summary: Defines pushforward distributions and the m-fold diagonal embedding. Proves image recovery and entropy invariance under any injective pushforward, diag injectivity for m at least 1, and the diagonal entropy equality that duplicated copies add no Shannon information.
files.conclusion: An m-fold diagonal copy with m at least 1 has the same Shannon entropy as the original.

files.summary: Proves a non-null record is emitted exactly for genuine distinctions and hence never on the diagonal. Packages record inertness with diagonal entropy invariance and the eqW void void fork as one fused trinity, witnessed on Bool with a fair coin flip.
files.conclusion: The same diagonal is record-inert, information-inert, and the rewrite fracture site.

files.summary: Proves the eqW diagonal disequality query has licensed-channel deficit exactly zero via the circular-reference theorem. Proves the direct residual is also zero and packages both with the eqW void void fork as the two faces of one echo vacuum.
files.conclusion: The eqW diagonal query has zero deficit, zero residual, and coincides with the rewrite fork.

files.summary: Defines bit entropy and uniform mass on a nonempty finite carrier. Proves uniform entropy equals log card, the Hartley envelope H ≤ log card with base-two form, Dirac zero, and product additivity in both units.
files.conclusion: Finite Shannon entropy is at most log card, attained by the uniform mass and additive on products.

files.summary: Carries a string-typed forced-trilemma anchor naming the refusal completeness substrate and manuscript thm:trilemma. Defines the three forced-output cases with exhaustiveness and proves no decisive payload-sensitive support on the recursor and on the fixed duplicating carrier.
files.conclusion: Every forced case is one of three and the unsupported-definite case has no decisive direct support.

files.summary: This file works on the two-outcome halt and loop star called starStep 2 as the smallest envelope that can host a halt-versus-loop query, with the echo channel as zero licensed evidence. It proves the echo deficit is zero, the Hartley entropy is one bit and the overproduction gap Omega is one, and it packages lowerBits one against evidenceUpperBits zero as a quantitative obstruction bridge that yields a boundary event. It shows the collapse schema only manufactures a decision procedure and is not Omega, that a resolving audit closes the same gap to zero, and that arity four yields two bits so the bound is carrier-specific.
files.conclusion: On the halt and loop star against zero echo evidence Omega equals one bit, while a resolving audit gives zero and arity four gives two bits, so the bound is carrier-specific and distinct from the decision procedure supplied by collapse.

files.summary: Defines direct and licensed conditional entropies and their difference as licensed-channel deficit. Proves nonnegativity, zero for channel-constant copies, exogeny for positive deficit, the two-sided bracket by the direct residual, and tightness for resolving channels with positive, zero, and saturating witnesses.
files.conclusion: Licensed deficit is sandwiched between zero and the direct residual, zero for copies and full for resolving channels.

files.summary: The file defines a LicensedCollapse over a finite verdict alphabet as a pre-license distribution with strictly positive Shannon entropy together with a determinate post-license verdict, and defines collapseDeficit as the pre-license entropy. It proves the deficit is positive before the license and that the entropy of the post-license point mass is zero. It proves the uniform distribution on Fin 2 has entropy Real.log 2 and builds two instances from it, confluenceCollapse with post-verdict 0 and terminationCollapse with post-verdict 1, with the confluence deficit shown to equal Real.log 2. It packages both instances in a unified collapse statement and records that the real-valued confluence deficit corresponds to the integer one-bit verdictBits collapse from BranchEntropy.
files.conclusion: Both the confluence and termination instances have strictly positive pre-license deficit with zero post-license residual, and the confluence deficit equals Real.log 2 while verdictBits 2 minus verdictBits 1 equals 1.

files.summary: Proves equality needs two held cells and no one-cell observer decides it, while two cells suffice. Proves the fair register has entropy log 2 and point masses have zero, re-exports the eqW fork, and proves the finite-carrier equivalence of distinction, two-cell necessity, and positive information with a Bool witness.
files.conclusion: On a finite carrier a distinction exists exactly when two-cell memory is necessary and a positive-information register exists.

files.summary: Models a query posterior as a finite sub-distribution with two positive-mass outcomes. Proves non-vacuity forces strictly positive conditional entropy and, under zero post-answer entropy, strictly positive mutual information.
files.conclusion: Every non-vacuous finite query has positive conditional entropy and positive information under sound answer.

files.summary: This file fixes the quotation diagonal quote of merge void void whose value void is already held on the direct surface, and it defines the observed Fin 2 outcome from the actual one-step evaluator together with the channel posterior as the point mass at that outcome. It proves the licensed-channel deficit is zero and the direct conditional entropy is zero, so the channel report is a redundant copy of the known value. It conjoins those vacuum facts with the rewrite-face nonjoinable quote and eval peak in one combined statement.
files.conclusion: The quotation diagonal has zero deficit and zero residual uncertainty on the information face while retaining a nonjoinable quote and eval peak on the rewrite face.

files.summary: Studies the counter-first relation on Nat pairs with its payload erasure. Proves every orienting measure is counter-dominated and no semantic measure is decisive and payload-sensitive on it.
files.conclusion: On iiRecursor no payload-sensitive decisive measure exists and orienting measures are counter-dominated.

files.summary: Defines an abstract jointly total positive and negative semidecider schema for any relation. Proves the schema manufactures a decision procedure by Nat.find, instantiates equality to DecidableEq, and ports the collapse to halting-style predicates.
files.conclusion: Any jointly total semidecider pair decides its relation, including equality and halting-style predicates.

files.summary: Defines minimal finite-alphabet Shannon entropy via negMulLog and the determinate point mass. Proves nonnegativity for sub-distributions, invariance under alphabet equivalence, and zero entropy for point masses.
files.conclusion: Finite entropy is nonnegative on sub-distributions, invariant under relabeling, and zero on point masses.

files.summary: This file defines a concrete RDRS step on Nat times Nat that fixes the counter and strictly decreases the payload with no payload erasure, together with the payload-projection measure. It proves the payload measure orients the step by s less than s plus one on every step, while any counter and base only payload-blind measure is constant on the step and cannot orient it. It obtains an orienting pair that is not counter-dominated, showing the PayloadErasure hypothesis is necessary.
files.conclusion: Some orienting semantic measure is not counter-dominated, so the PayloadErasure hypothesis cannot be dropped.

files.summary: Distinguishes verdict uncertainty from witness uncertainty with soundness and sound-supported priors. Proves a termination proof forces every sound verdict to true, the induced marginal is a point mass, and its entropy is zero. Specializes to the KO7 recursor with a canonical prior.
files.conclusion: A proved terminating cell has zero verdict entropy under every normalized sound-supported prior, including the KO7 recursor.

files.summary: This file is a paired reach and axiom gate for CountableRoleExchange. It checks countable role divergence with fintype and uniform versions, term bounds and nonnegativity lemmas. It also checks self-divergence and recovery of finite role exchange.
files.conclusion: Countable role divergence is nonnegative, zero on self and recovers finite exchange.

files.summary: This reach gate audits EchoStoppingMDP across deterministic, horizon and stochastic layers without adding definitions. It checks stopping MDP structure, continuation and compute advantages, dynamic and horizon policies with value theory, and echo-license stopping lemmas. It also checks stochastic Bellman theory with averaging fixtures and proves three examples for attainment, empty actions and the 3/2 adaptive policy.
files.conclusion: Optimal stopping values are attained and the averaging fixture witnesses a 3/2 adaptive value.

files.summary: This file is a reach gate for nine gap-closure modules with axiom audits. It prints axioms for mass-profile identity and separation failure, LCEL collisions and repaired schemas, size-change soundness, nonvacuous closures, record emission, terminal-decoder scope, description gaps, proof length by size, and determination and provenance limits. It defines no new objects and proves no new theorems.
files.conclusion: All headline gap-closure theorems elaborate within the propext, choice and quotient baseline.

files.summary: This file is a paired reachability and axiom check for OverproductionGapChainRule. It checks incremental gain bits, the evidence chain rule, equality of omega drop with incremental gain, antitonicity in licensed gain, strict drop with strict gain, and the fork-echo to resolving chain rule. No new definitions or theorems are declared.
files.conclusion: The file confirms that every named OverproductionGapChainRule declaration is reachable and reports its axioms without adding new content.

files.summary: This file checks reachability and axioms for general role exchange. It covers role weights, role-resolving mixtures, general value-blind and role gaps, exchange and nonnegativity and zero-characterization results, finite-relation specializations, and uniform-frame entropy lemmas. It also checks the dependency-pair channel calculations, one-bit exchange, full resolution closure, and the rary occurrence separation from value-factoring. No new definitions or theorems are declared.
files.conclusion: The file confirms that every named general role-exchange declaration is reachable and reports its axioms without adding new content.

files.summary: This file is a reachability check for the m-ary role-exchange module and proves no new content. It checks star-step reachability, terminal normality and support and entropy, zero-source behavior, uniform role weights, role echo and role resolving channels, and logarithmic gap calculations. It also checks mixture, entropy, deficit and zero-gap results culminating in m-ary exchange and the binary case. No new definitions or theorems are declared.
files.conclusion: The file confirms that every named m-ary role-exchange declaration is reachable and reports its axioms while proving no new content.

files.summary: This file checks reachability and axioms for the Shannon overproduction-gap module. It covers terminal points and schedulers, entropy definitions, the Shannon gap and its Hartley bound, uniform schedulers attaining Hartley entropy, and licensed-entropy alignment with zero-residual closure. It also checks fork-three uniform gap values and the Shannon law. No new definitions or theorems are declared.
files.conclusion: The file confirms that every named Shannon-gap declaration elaborates and reports its axioms without adding new content.

files.summary: This file checks the execution-derived recursor stopping law with paired `#check` and `#print axioms`. It covers rary and binary cumulative and marginal costs, cutoff specifications and ties, stopping models with Bellman identities and finite-horizon maxima, optimal stopping-time existence, after-cutoff optimality and constant-benefit and zero-cost controls. Fourteen `decide` and rewriting examples evaluate exact costs, cutoffs and control values.
files.conclusion: The recursor stopping law is complete with an attainable optimal policy crown separating stopping from continuation by cutoff.

files.summary: This file checks reachability of the reflective dependency-pairs module. It runs paired #check and #print axioms for the obligation carrier, meta-query state with constructors and projections, rank and licensed relation, well-foundedness, blocked identities, cycle descent, and the three-state deliberation demo with unlicensed rank-tie examples. It proves no new content.
files.conclusion: The file pins the rank-licensed reflective-step surface and its blocked identity and tie cases.

files.summary: This file checks payload-generic role split and role-gap divergence. It runs paired #check and #print axioms for payload projections, two-action boundaries and sameness, exogenous separators and recursor instances, surjectivity, KL from uniform with term-split and entropy form, general and finite-relation gap equalities, nonnegativity and zero-iff-uniform. It proves no new content.
files.conclusion: The file pins payload role-split facts with the KL-based gap characterization.

files.summary: This file checks reachability of the role-split law. It runs paired #check and #print axioms for value-factored predicates, separator non-factoring, diagonal refusal, value blindness, trichotomy, role splits, boolean separators, two-action boundaries with refusal, lifting and exogeneity, value projections and recursor instances, and one-bit supply. It proves no new content.
files.conclusion: The file pins the role-split law with diagonal refusal and one-bit lift.

files.summary: This file defines no new mathematical objects and proves no theorems. It performs paired reachability and axiom checks for the ZeroDeficitStopping module, issuing one #check and one #print axioms command for each public declaration including structures, constructors, projections, loss functions, expectations, optimal policy, zero-deficit results, and demonstration channels. It therefore verifies that every listed name resolves and its axiom dependencies can be displayed.
files.conclusion: Every listed ZeroDeficitStopping declaration is reachable by #check and its axiom dependencies can be displayed.
